finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Providing a specially crafted filename that includes shell metacharacters
finding.assumptions: The program is intended to read from a file, but the filename is directly passed to `inFile.open()`. If the filename is attacker-controlled, it could potentially lead to command injection if the program is run in a vulnerable environment.

finding.title: Infinite Loop
finding.trigger: Providing an empty file or a file with unexpected EOF behavior
finding.assumptions: The loop condition checks `inFile.eof()` after attempting to read from the file. This can lead to an infinite loop if the file is empty or if the EOF is not correctly detected.

finding.title: Unvalidated Input
finding.trigger: Providing non-string input or unexpected input patterns
finding.assumptions: The input words are directly read from `std::cin` without any validation. This can lead to unexpected behavior if the input is not as expected.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.trigger: Providing a word with a length that exceeds the expected bounds
finding.assumptions: The loop iterates over the length of the word. If the word length is not properly validated, it could lead to a buffer overflow if the word is manipulated to be longer than expected.
